chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, God — Blessed and Exalted — created the world in six days, then He subtracted those from the days of the year; and the year is three hundred and fifty-four (354) days. Sha'ban will never be complete, ever; Ramadan will never be deficient — by God — ever! And an obligation (fard) can never be deficient.
Indeed, God — Mighty and Majestic — says: 'and that you complete the number' (Quran 2:185)
And Shawwal is twenty-nine days. And Dhu al-Qa'dah is thirty days,
due to the Words of God — Mighty and Majestic: 'And We appointed with Musa thirty nights and completed them with ten, so the appointed time of his Lord was complete: forty nights' (Quran 7:142)
And Dhu al-Hijjah is twenty-nine days. And al-Muharram is thirty days. Then the months after that alternate: a complete month and a deficient month.

key_terms.اخْتَزَلَهَا: to subtract/reduce — the six days of creation are removed from the year's total, giving 354 days
key_terms.تَامٌّ وَنَاقِصٌ: complete and deficient — the alternating pattern of 30-day and 29-day months in the Islamic calendar
key_terms.فَرِيضَةٌ نَاقِصَةً: deficient obligation — a religious duty cannot be properly fulfilled if the prescribed month is incomplete
key_terms.مِيقَاتُ: appointed time or place — used for Moses's forty nights and later for the pilgrim's station in Hajj

ai.seo_question: Why is Ramadan always 30 days and Sha'ban always 29 days according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) explains the theological and jurisprudential basis for the Islamic lunar calendar, teaching that God created the world in six days and then deducted those six days from the year's count, resulting in a 354-day year. He establishes divine principles for the calendar: Sha'ban is always 29 days (never complete), and Ramadan is always 30 days (never deficient), grounding these rules in Quranic injunctions and the narrative of Prophet Musa's forty-night appointment with God. The Imam provides this teaching in the context of Islamic jurisprudence on fasting and religious obligations, which cannot be fulfilled with incomplete months.
